info.title: SOVA API
info.summary: REST API for the SOVA multitenant issue tracker.
info.description: The contract starts with the technical foundation endpoints and is extended together with every API implementation checkpoint.

get.summary: Get API metadata

200.description: The credentials were verified and session cookies were issued.

Set-Cookie.description: The HttpOnly session and readable CSRF cookies.

get.summary: Get the current authenticated identity
get.description: Restores the effective user profile, explicit SUPERADMIN context and optional session-bound impersonation. No credential or session token is returned.

post.description: Always returns the same accepted response for a syntactically valid email, regardless of account existence or recovery throttling.

202.description: The recovery request was accepted without disclosing account existence.

post.summary: Set a new password using a one-time token

204.description: The password was replaced and all existing sessions were revoked.

post.description: Always returns the same accepted response for a syntactically valid email, regardless of account existence, account state, or throttling.

202.description: The request was accepted without disclosing account existence or state.

post.summary: Verify an email using a one-time token

200.description: The email is verified. Reusing the same consumed token is idempotent.

post.description: The token is sent in the request body so reverse-proxy access logs do not contain it.

200.description: Safe invitation details for the token holder.

post.summary: Create a verified account from an invitation
post.description: This is the only public account-creation operation. User, verified email, active membership, and consumed invitation are committed atomically.

201.description: The verified user and active membership were created.

post.summary: Accept an invitation with the authenticated account

200.description: The invitation was accepted for the matching account.

204.description: The current session was revoked and its cookies were cleared.

get.summary: List active sessions for the current user

delete.summary: Revoke one session owned by the current user

get.summary: List tenants for system administration
get.description: Requires the current separate SUPERADMIN system role. Returns every non-deleted tenant with lifecycle revision and administrative metadata.

post.summary: Create a pending tenant and invite its first owner
post.description: Requires SUPERADMIN. Creates the tenant, provisions immutable default roles and publishes a TENANT_OWNER invitation atomically. The tenant becomes ACTIVE when that invitation is accepted. Reusing the same Idempotency-Key and body safely replays the result.

200.description: An earlier successful request with the same idempotency key was replayed.

201.description: The pending tenant and owner invitation were created.

patch.description: Requires SUPERADMIN, a reason and the current optimistic revision. Direct transition to DELETED is unavailable; DELETION_PENDING starts a 30-day grace period and can be cancelled back to ARCHIVED.

200.description: The tenant is in the requested status.

get.summary: List every global user account
get.description: Requires system.users.manage. Access itself is appended to the security audit.

patch.summary: Change a global user account status
patch.description: Requires system.users.manage. Only ACTIVE and DISABLED are accepted as targets; PENDING_VERIFICATION and LOCKED may still transition into either through the existing account state machine. Own account changes are rejected, and disabling the last active superadmin's account is rejected.

200.description: The user account is in the requested status.

put.description: Requires system.superadmins.manage. Repeating an existing grant is idempotent.

200.description: The user holds the SUPERADMIN role.

delete.description: Requires system.superadmins.manage. Rejects revoking your own role and rejects removing the last active superadmin. Repeating a missing grant is idempotent.

200.description: The user no longer holds the SUPERADMIN role.

get.summary: List immutable system security audit events
get.description: Requires system.audit.view. SUPERADMIN receives a newest-first keyset page across system and tenant contexts. Access to this endpoint is itself appended to the audit.

200.description: A newest-first page of immutable security audit events.

post.description: Requires system.impersonate through the non-impersonated SUPERADMIN context, the current administrator password, a support reason, an active target membership and an active tenant. The context is bound to the current server session and expires after at most 15 minutes.

201.description: The effective identity was switched to the selected tenant user.

delete.description: Ends an active, expired or invalidated impersonation on the current server session and restores the real actor identity.

get.summary: List tenants accessible to the current user
get.description: Regular users receive only active tenants backed by an active membership. SUPERADMIN receives every non-deleted tenant without requiring membership.

200.description: Tenants available to the authenticated session.

get.summary: Resolve an authorized tenant context
get.description: The tenant identifier comes from the route. A foreign, inactive, deleted, or otherwise inaccessible tenant is returned as not found. SUPERADMIN may explicitly enter every non-deleted tenant and that access is audited.

200.description: The requested tenant context is accessible.

post.summary: Create and queue a tenant invitation
post.description: Requires tenant.members.invite or the SUPERADMIN bypass. The plaintext token is never returned by the API.

201.description: The invitation and encrypted delivery event were created.

get.summary: List immutable security events for one tenant
get.description: Requires tenant.audit.view in the route-derived tenant context. Events from every other tenant are excluded in the repository query. Access to this endpoint is itself appended to the tenant audit.

200.description: A newest-first page containing only this tenant's immutable security events.

get.summary: Export immutable security events for one tenant as CSV
get.description: Requires tenant.audit.export in the route-derived tenant context. Applies the same filters and redaction as the list endpoint, internally follows the keyset cursor up to a bounded row cap, and returns a single CSV attachment instead of a paginated JSON page. The export itself is appended to the tenant audit.

200.description: A CSV attachment containing up to 5000 newest-first matching events.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for the CSV export.

get.summary: List every workgroup in a tenant
get.description: Requires tenant.workgroups.manage.

post.description: Requires tenant.workgroups.manage.

patch.description: Requires tenant.workgroups.manage, or workgroup.manage on this specific workgroup. ACTIVE and ARCHIVED toggle in either direction; repeating the current status is idempotent.

200.description: The workgroup is in the requested status.

get.summary: List the members of a workgroup
get.description: Requires tenant.workgroups.manage, or workgroup.view on this specific workgroup.

put.summary: Add a workgroup member or change their role
put.description: Requires tenant.workgroups.manage, or workgroup.members.manage on this specific workgroup. The tenant membership must be active. Idempotent when the member already holds the requested role.

200.description: The membership holds the requested workgroup role.

delete.description: Requires tenant.workgroups.manage, or workgroup.members.manage on this specific workgroup. Repeating a missing membership is idempotent.

204.description: The membership is no longer part of the workgroup.

get.summary: List every project in a tenant
get.description: Requires tenant.projects.manage.

post.description: Requires tenant.projects.create. A private project requires lead_membership_id, which is assigned PROJECT_MANAGER.

patch.description: Requires tenant.projects.manage, or project.settings.manage on this specific project. ACTIVE and ARCHIVED toggle in either direction; repeating the current status is idempotent.

200.description: The project is in the requested status.

get.summary: List the roles defined for a project
get.description: Requires tenant.projects.manage, or project.view on this specific project.

200.description: Every role defined for the project.

get.summary: List the members of a project
get.description: Requires tenant.projects.manage, or project.view on this specific project.

200.description: Every member of the project, with their assigned roles.

put.summary: Assign a project role to a tenant membership
put.description: Requires tenant.projects.manage, or project.members.manage on this specific project. The tenant membership and the project role must both be active. Idempotent when the membership already holds the role.

204.description: The membership holds the project role.

delete.summary: Remove a project role from a tenant membership
delete.description: Requires tenant.projects.manage, or project.members.manage on this specific project. Repeating a missing assignment is idempotent.

204.description: The membership no longer holds the project role.

get.summary: List the workgroups linked to a project
get.description: Requires tenant.projects.manage, or project.view on this specific project.

200.description: Every workgroup linked to the project, with its granted role.

put.summary: Link a workgroup to a project or change its role
put.description: Requires tenant.projects.manage, or project.members.manage on this specific project. The workgroup and the project role must both be active. Upserts the role when the workgroup is already linked.

204.description: The workgroup is linked to the project with the requested role.

delete.summary: Unlink a workgroup from a project
delete.description: Requires tenant.projects.manage, or project.members.manage on this specific project. Repeating a missing link is idempotent.

204.description: The workgroup is no longer linked to the project.

get.summary: List tenant roles and assignable permission definitions
get.description: Requires tenant.roles.view. System-scoped permissions are never returned as tenant-role options.

200.description: Tenant roles and the non-system permission catalog.

post.description: Requires tenant.roles.manage. The immutable role code must be unique within the tenant. Only non-system permissions may be selected and all catalog dependencies must be included.

201.description: The custom tenant role was created.

put.description: Requires tenant.roles.manage. The role code and system roles are immutable. The complete non-system permission set is replaced after validating dependencies, and revision provides optimistic concurrency control.

200.description: The custom tenant role was updated.

delete.summary: Archive an unassigned custom tenant role
delete.description: Requires tenant.roles.manage. System roles cannot be archived, and a custom role must first be removed from every membership. Repeating the archive of an already archived custom role is idempotent.

204.description: The custom tenant role is archived.

get.summary: List tenant memberships and their tenant roles
get.description: Requires tenant.members.view. The administrative list includes active, disabled, and removed memberships; it never exposes password data.

200.description: Tenant memberships with user identity and assigned tenant roles.

patch.summary: Change a tenant membership lifecycle status
patch.description: Requires tenant.members.manage. ACTIVE may transition to DISABLED or REMOVED, DISABLED may transition to ACTIVE or REMOVED, and REMOVED is terminal. Own membership changes are blocked. Any membership holding TENANT_OWNER additionally requires tenant.roles.manage and the last active owner can never be deactivated or removed.

200.description: The membership is in the requested status. Repeating the current status is idempotent.

put.summary: Assign a tenant role to an active membership
put.description: Requires tenant.roles.assign. Assigning TENANT_OWNER additionally requires tenant.roles.manage. Repeating an existing assignment is idempotent.

delete.summary: Remove a tenant role from a membership
delete.description: Requires tenant.roles.assign. Removing TENANT_OWNER additionally requires tenant.roles.manage and cannot remove the last active tenant owner. Repeating a missing assignment is idempotent.

204.description: The tenant role is not assigned to the membership.

get.summary: Check API liveness
get.description: Alias of the dedicated liveness endpoint. It does not check external dependencies.

get.summary: Check API liveness
Check API and PostgreSQL readiness

200.description: The API and all required dependencies are ready.

503.description: At least one required dependency is not ready.

get.summary: List the newest issues of a project
get.description: Requires `issue.view` on the project. A convenience listing capped at a fixed size; the full, filtered view is the SovaQL search.

200.description: The most recent issues of the project.

post.description: Requires `issue.create` on the project. The key is `CODE-number` from an atomic per-project counter; the initial status comes from the type's published workflow, never from the client. An archived project answers `409 PROJECT_ARCHIVED`.

Requires a session. The tenant, the caller's projects and `issue.view` are applied **before** the compiled filter, so no query fragment can widen the scope; an empty scope returns an empty page rather than `403`. Paging is a signed keyset cursor that only walks forward.

post.summary: Check a SovaQL query without running it
post.description: Validation is server-side on purpose: a second grammar in the client would drift from the language. Errors carry a stable code, a localisation key and a range in UTF-8 code points. `basic_form` projects the query onto what the visual builder can draw, and says `representable: false` rather than silently simplifying it.

200.description: The verdict, with every error at once.

get.summary: List queryable fields and the active limits
get.description: Only fields whose storage exists are listed, so the editor never advertises one that would be rejected, nor a limit operations has since changed.

get.summary: Get one issue
get.description: Requires `issue.view` on the issue's project. An issue in another tenant or an unreachable project answers `404`, never `403`.

get.summary: List the transitions available right now
get.description: Only transitions legal for the current status and workflow version that the caller may run, including runtime rule conditions. The response carries the issue version the offer was computed against.

post.summary: Move an issue through a transition
post.description: Requires `issue.transition` plus whatever the transition's rules demand. The client names the **transition**, never the target status, and sends the version the offer was computed against — a concurrent change answers `409 ISSUE_VERSION_CONFLICT`. History and the outbox event are written in the same transaction.

post.summary: Change the type of an issue
post.description: Requires `issue.change-type`. The target type must be active with a published workflow, the hierarchy must still hold for the parent and existing children, and the current status is mapped into the target workflow — when that is ambiguous the API asks for `target_status_id` with `409 ISSUE_TYPE_STATUS_MAPPING_REQUIRED`.

200.description: The issue under its new type.

get.summary: Read the user-visible history of an issue
get.description: Requires `issue.view`. This is the activity trail people read, separate from the append-only security audit.

get.summary: List the comments of an issue
get.description: Requires `issue.view`. Bodies are CommonMark **source**; the API never returns HTML.

post.description: Requires `comment.create`. Raw HTML is refused at the boundary, though fenced blocks and code spans are left alone. A mention is a Markdown link to a membership and **grants nothing**: everybody mentioned must already hold `issue.view`, otherwise `422 COMMENT_MENTION_NOT_ALLOWED`.

patch.description: The author may edit within the edit window; afterwards it takes `comment.moderate`.

delete.description: A soft, idempotent removal: the comment keeps its place in the discussion but loses its text and its mentions.

get.summary: List who watches an issue
get.description: Requires `issue.view`. The reason each person is subscribed is returned, so the automatic rules stay visible instead of feeling like magic.

200.description: Watchers and whether the caller is one.

put.description: A member manages only their own subscription, so there is no identifier in the path.

delete.description: An explicit unsubscribe is a stored decision: it survives the automatic rules, which never re-subscribe somebody who opted out.

get.summary: List the links of an issue
get.description: Both sides are filtered through the caller's `issue.view` scope, so a link to something they cannot see does not appear.

200.description: Links, seen from this issue's side.

post.description: Requires `issue.edit` on the issue's project. Stored once and read from both sides, so the directions cannot contradict each other. A cross-tenant link is not representable, a self-link is `422` and an existing pair in either direction is `409`.

get.summary: List the attachments of an issue
get.description: Requires `issue.view`. The storage key is deliberately absent: publishing it would invite callers to build their own paths to the bytes.

post.summary: Attach a file to an issue
post.description: Requires `attachment.upload`. `multipart/form-data` with one file per request. The media type is sniffed from the bytes and matched against an allowlist — an extension may narrow the verdict, never widen it — and the size is measured on disk, not taken from the request. Without a configured scanner the file is stored as `SKIPPED`, never as a pretended `CLEAN`.

get.summary: Download an attachment
get.description: Authorised on every call — there is no public or pre-signed URL. The response is always `Content-Disposition: attachment` with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, so user bytes are never rendered inline. Only `CLEAN` and `SKIPPED` files are served.

delete.description: Requires `attachment.delete` or ownership. The record survives for retention; the bytes go immediately.

get.summary: Read a project's issue types, statuses and workflows
get.description: Requires `project.view`. The revision is the optimistic lock for publishing.

get.summary: Read the configuration change log
get.description: Requires `project.settings.manage`. Newest first.

get.summary: List the workflows of a project
get.description: Requires `project.view`. Each workflow carries its published version and its single draft, if one exists.

post.summary: Open a draft from the published version
post.description: Requires `project.settings.manage`. At most one draft per workflow, enforced by a partial unique index; a second attempt answers `409 WORKFLOW_DRAFT_EXISTS`.

put.summary: Replace the contents of the draft
put.description: Requires `project.settings.manage` and the draft's `expected_version` — a stale one answers `409 WORKFLOW_DRAFT_CONFLICT`. The draft governs membership, transitions and the initial status only; status attributes are project-wide, so editing a draft never changes the published version.

get.summary: Check the draft's graph
get.description: Reachability, at least one `DONE` status and one primary action per status.

get.summary: See what publishing the draft would do
get.description: Added and removed statuses and transitions, how many issues each affected status carries, and which removed statuses need a migration target.

post.description: Requires `project.settings.manage`. One transaction: the configuration revision is checked (`409 PROJECT_CONFIG_VERSION_CONFLICT`), the graph revalidated (`422 WORKFLOW_INVALID`), the active version switched and every issue migrated onto it. A removed status that still carries issues needs `status_mapping` (`409 WORKFLOW_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`); a target outside the new version is `422 WORKFLOW_MIGRATION_TARGET_INVALID`.

get.summary: List the saved queries the caller may open
get.description: Their own, plus those shared with them or with a workgroup they belong to. Visibility is computed in the same SQL that reads the row, so a query they may not see never leaves the database.

post.description: Requires `saved-query.create`. Only a query the language accepts is stored, and the canonical form is produced by the server. New queries are private until shared.

get.summary: Get one saved query
get.description: Somebody else's private query is not forbidden, it is invisible: `404`, not `403`.

patch.description: Needs `EDIT` access. Visibility is not in the body, so editing somebody else's shared query can never publish it further, and the name is checked against the **owner's** names, not the editor's.

post.description: Owner or `saved-query.manage` only — holding `EDIT` is enough to change a query, never to withdraw it from everybody else. Archiving frees the name. A query a dashboard widget still renders answers `409 SAVED_QUERY_IN_USE` with the number of dependants in `detail`.

get.summary: List who else holds this query
get.description: Reaching the query is the gate; who else holds it is something its readers may know.

put.summary: Replace the whole set of grants
put.description: Requires `saved-query.share`. The complete set is sent, because a partial edit cannot guarantee that an omitted principal really loses access; visibility is derived from the result. **Sharing is not access**: a grant lets somebody run the query, never see an issue they otherwise could not — results are intersected with the reader's own `issue.view` scope on every run.

put.summary: Mark a query as a favourite
put.description: A personal link between the caller's membership and the query, not a property of the query.

200.description: The query, no longer a favourite.

get.summary: Read the caller's inbox
get.description: Only its owner reads it: there is no identifier in the path, and every command is keyed by the caller's membership. A caller acting purely on system power has no membership and therefore an empty inbox, not an error.

post.description: An empty list marks the whole inbox read.

200.description: How many changed, and what remains unread.

get.summary: Read the caller's notification settings
get.description: Per member and event kind. Only real choices are stored; the rest are filled in from the defaults, so a new event kind needs no backfill.

put.description: The in-app channel is locked on for assignment and mention — enforced in the domain, not in the HTTP layer. Email is off everywhere by default.

get.summary: List the caller's own dashboards
get.description: A dashboard is personal: only the owner's are returned, and the response names which one to open — the last they looked at, or their default when that preference is missing or points at something since deleted. A member who owns no dashboard yet is given the starter one here (spec §7.2): every active member must have at least one. It writes only when there is nothing at all, and it leaves the active preference alone — the new dashboard is their default, which an empty preference resolves to anyway. Nothing is provisioned for a caller without `dashboard.create`.

200.description: The dashboards and which one to open.

post.description: Requires `dashboard.create`. The first dashboard a member owns becomes their default.

post.summary: Build a dashboard from the system starter template
post.description: Requires `dashboard.create`, `dashboard.update-own` and `saved-query.create`. Creates a dashboard from the shipped starter manifest in one transaction: private saved queries owned by the caller, the widgets that render them and the layout. Restoring **adds** — it never overwrites. Existing dashboards, widgets and queries are untouched, the default flag stays where the member put it and the active preference is not moved. A name already in use is resolved by counting up rather than by refusing.

201.description: The new dashboard and the widgets the template put on it.

get.summary: Get one dashboard
get.description: Somebody else's dashboard is not forbidden, it is absent: `404`, so the endpoint cannot be used to learn that it exists.

delete.description: Requires `dashboard.delete-own`. The last one stays — a member must always have one, and emptying it is the way to start over (`409 LAST_DASHBOARD_REQUIRED`). Deleting the default passes the flag to the next in order.

put.description: Exactly one dashboard is the default; the move happens in one transaction behind a partial unique index rather than by trusting whoever remembers to clear the previous one.

put.summary: Remember which dashboard the caller last opened
put.description: An explicit request on purpose: a prefetch or a link preview must never move where somebody lands next, so this is never a side effect of a `GET`.

200.description: The dashboard, now the active one.

post.summary: Duplicate a dashboard with its widgets
post.description: Requires `dashboard.create`. The copy carries the same widgets in the same places and points at the **same** saved queries — duplicating those as well would quietly double the member's query list every time they copied a dashboard. The copy never inherits the default flag.

get.summary: List the widgets of a dashboard
get.description: Unreachable dashboards answer `404` before any widget rule is consulted.

post.description: Requires `dashboard.update-own`. The widget must name a saved query the caller can already open, otherwise `404 WIDGET_DATA_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND` — a dashboard is not a way to run somebody else's private query. The configuration is rebuilt key by key from what the type declares, so an unknown key never reaches storage. A new widget lands under everything already there.

patch.description: The type is fixed for the life of the instance: changing it would reinterpret a configuration written for a different schema.

put.summary: Apply a whole arrangement at once
put.description: One request rather than one per widget: moving two widgets past each other is only legal as a pair. The body must place **every** widget of the dashboard, and the server checks bounds, per-type sizes and overlap across the whole set. A stale `expected_version` answers `409 DASHBOARD_VERSION_CONFLICT` and **nothing moves**.

200.description: The widgets in their new places.

get.summary: Load the data behind one widget
get.description: Each widget is loaded separately, so one unreachable source does not blank the whole page. The saved query runs **as the caller**: the scope is applied before any aggregation, because a total over rows somebody cannot see would disclose them just as surely as returning them. The source is re-checked on every load, so a revoked grant answers `404 WIDGET_DATA_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND` at once.

200.description: The widget's data, shaped by its type.

get.summary: List the widget types this deployment ships
get.description: A **data** registry: keys, schema versions, sizes and aggregation dimensions. It carries no component name and nothing executable; the client maps a `type_key` to a component itself. Labels are localisation keys, so no wording ships from the server.

sessionCookie.name: sova_session
sessionCookie.description: Opaque server-session token. The cookie is HttpOnly.

csrfHeader.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfHeader.description: Token copied from the readable sova_csrf cookie for unsafe requests.

AuditCursor.name: cursor
AuditCursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor returned as next_cursor by the previous page.

Problem.description: A request error represented as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

is_superadmin.description: True only when the user currently holds the separate SUPERADMIN system role.

next_cursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor for the next page, or null at the end.

membership_id.description: Active membership identifier, or null when access is granted by SUPERADMIN.

code.description: Stable tenant-local role identifier. It cannot be changed or reused after archival.

permissions.description: Complete set of non-system permission codes, including every declared dependency.
Complete replacement set of non-system permission codes, including every declared dependency.

revision.description: Revision returned by the most recent role read.

request_id.description: Correlation identifier matching the X-Request-ID header.

code.description: Stable machine-readable generic or domain error code.

errors.description: Optional field error map for validation problems.

description.description: CommonMark **source**. The API never returns rendered HTML.

version.description: Optimistic lock. Send it back with every change.

query.description: SovaQL. An empty query means everything the caller may see.

oneOf.description: Signed keyset cursor from a previous page. It is bound to the tenant, the effective user, the authorisation revision, the canonical query and the sort, so it cannot be replayed against a different search.

message_key.description: Localisation key the client resolves; the server ships no wording.

representable.description: False when the query uses `OR`, `NOT` or parentheses, which the basic builder cannot draw. The UI then shows it read-only rather than silently simplifying it.

fields.description: Only the fields whose storage exists today.

issue_version.description: The version the offer was computed against; send it back when executing.

fields.description: Values a rule declared as required.

media_type.description: Sniffed from the bytes, never taken from the client.

downloadable.description: `CLEAN` and `SKIPPED` only. `SKIPPED` means stored without a scan.

relation.description: What the link means from the open issue's side, e.g. `IS_BLOCKED_BY`, so the client never has to work the direction out itself.

source.description: Why they are subscribed; the automatic rules stay visible.

watching.description: Whether the caller watches this issue.

key.description: A key from the application's rule catalogue, e.g. `permission`, `assignee_or_manager`, `resolution_required`, `set_resolution`.

revision.description: Monotonic per project; send it as `expected_config_version` when publishing.

statuses.description: Draft membership only: status attributes are project-wide entities.

required_status_mapping_codes.description: Removed statuses that still carry issues; publishing needs a target for each.

status_mapping.description: Removed status code → target status id in the new version.

viewer_access.description: What *this* caller may do; the same row answers differently per reader.

query.description: SovaQL; only a query the language accepts is stored.

grants.description: The complete set. A principal left out loses access.

items.description: Exactly one principal: a membership or a workgroup, never both and never neither.

payload.description: Issue key and title; never comment text.

notification_ids.description: Empty marks the whole inbox read.

in_app_locked.description: Assignment and mention always reach the in-app inbox.

is_active.description: Which one the caller last opened — a preference of theirs, not a property of the row.

name.description: Unique per owner, compared case- and whitespace-insensitively.
Optional. Defaults to the manifest's name; a name already used by one of the caller's own dashboards is suffixed with a counter.

available.description: False when this deployment no longer knows the stored type; the row is still returned so it can be removed.

configuration.description: Validated against the schema of its type; unknown keys never reach storage.

widgets.description: Every widget of the dashboard: a partial layout is how two end up overlapping.

dimensions.description: Fields this type may aggregate by.

points.description: Empty buckets are zero, never a missing point.

code.description: Short project code; the prefix of every issue key.

visibility.description: Enforced on read, not merely stored: a `PRIVATE` project is listed only for members who hold a role on it directly or through a linked workgroup.

viewer_roles.description: The role codes the caller holds on this project.

status.description: Archiving is reversible and idempotent; an archived project grants no project permission.

UpsertProjectWorkgroupRequest.description: Links the workgroup to one project role; every member of the group gets its permissions.
